title: 🏛️ Exam 2024 general · reading: a young blind pianist ⭐⭐

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, general — reading, question 1)
A text is about Chapman Shum, a 13-year-old boy who is blind and plays the piano.

The text is mainly about a boy who has

options.text: learned music to entertain himself
won a national piano competition against adults
played music since he was a baby
used music to affect people's lives

questions.explanation: The text shows Chapman using music to build his own confidence, to inspire others at charity concerts and to set an example for children with difficulties. That is using music to affect people's lives. He started the piano at five, not as a baby, and his aim is to inspire others, not only to entertain himself. No competition against adults is mentioned.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, general — reading, question 2a, paragraph 1)
The first paragraph presents Chapman Shum, a blind 13-year-old with speech and learning difficulties. Judge the statement below against what it says.

"Chapman learned his first piano lessons with a teacher."

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 tells how Chapman's love of music began and how he started to play. The statement is false.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, general — reading, question 2a, paragraph 1)
A student says: "Chapman learned his first piano lessons with a teacher." Which part of paragraph 1 settles whether this statement is true or false?

options.text: passed the grade 8 piano exam
showcase his talent all over Britain
he taught himself to play the piano
a rare disease that caused his blindness

questions.explanation: At the age of five Chapman taught himself to play the piano, so he had no teacher for his first lessons. Passing the grade 8 exam and playing around Britain come later and do not say who taught him.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, general — reading, question 2b, paragraph 3)
The last paragraph deals with the boy's goal and with the award he won in 2023. Judge the statement below against what it says.

"Chapman wants other children to learn from his experience with music."

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 explains Chapman's goal. He wants more than an audience for his music. The statement is true.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, general — reading, question 2b, paragraph 3)
A student says: "Chapman wants other children to learn from his experience with music." Which part of paragraph 3 settles whether this statement is true or false?

options.text: the transformative effects of music on individuals with handicaps
set an example to other children who have learning difficulties
nominated Young Person of the Year in 2023
His journey is an inspiring one

questions.explanation: Chapman's goal is to set an example to other children who have learning difficulties: other children can learn from what he did. The other parts describe the effects of music, his award or his story, not what he wants for other children.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, general — reading, question 3, paragraph 1)
Paragraph 1 says: "He passed the grade 8 piano exam with flying colors."

What does this sentence nearly mean?

options.text: He prepared well for the exam.
He had excellent exam results.
He could draw colored pictures.

questions.explanation: "With flying colors" is an expression: you pass an exam with flying colors when your results are excellent. It does not talk about real colors or drawing, and the sentence says nothing about how he prepared.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, general — reading, question 4, paragraph 2)
Paragraph 2 says: "He hopes his journey will show the incredible benefits of music and how it can offer a unique opportunity for communication and self-expression..."

What does "it" refer to?

options.text: the incredible benefits
a unique opportunity
Chapman
music

questions.explanation: Put the noun back: how music can offer a unique opportunity for communication and self-expression. "It" is singular, so it cannot be "the benefits", and it cannot be a person like Chapman. "A unique opportunity" is what is offered, so it comes after the pronoun.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024, general — reading, question 5)
The exam asks: "Do you agree that music can have a positive effect on the school results of the disabled people? Why? Why not?" Think about a student who says YES.

Which arguments does the text support?

options.text: Music gives Chapman motivation and self-confidence.
Music cures the disease that caused his blindness.
Music offers children with special needs a way to communicate and express themselves.
Chapman stopped having learning difficulties after his first concert.
Chapman prefers music to school, so he left school.

questions.explanation: The text says music is a source of motivation and self-confidence for Chapman and a unique opportunity for communication and self-expression for children with special needs who may fail to do well at school. It never says that music cures his disease, that his difficulties disappeared or that he left school.
